8th Vote of No Confidence for President Zuma

By: Liz Fish | Production

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
This is President Jacob Zuma 8th vote of no confidence in his 8 years of Presidency. What set this one apart from previous motions was the massive civil society mobilization behind the call for Zuma to go and this was the first to be conducted in secret. In June The Constitution Court ruled that the Speaker did have the discretion to decide on a secret ballot.




Summary:
Despite this ruling the Speaker held the opposition and country in suspense to the last moment announcing on Monday to everyone’s surprise that it would be held in secret. Civil society took to the streets under a united banner #Unite Behind calling for Zuma to go. Allegations that the State has been captured have been overwhelmingly corroborated in the last few weeks by the body of evidence in the Gupta Leaks, making the Nkandla scandal pail into insignificance.
The Opposition Parties maintained in Parliament on the 8th that they were not attacking the ANC but simply want Zuma to be removed. The ANC saw the motion of no confidence as an attack on the ANC and an election ploy on behalf of the opposition. It was notable that all arguments from the ANC in Parliament on Tuesday were in defense of the ANC and not of Jacob Zuma. Fear mongering prevailed and the motion of no confidence was even called an attempted Coup d’etat. The results surprised everyone and were far closer than expected - 177 against Zuma, 198 for Zuma, and 9 abstentions which can be considered as a vote against Zuma but not the ANC. For the first time ever ANC members voted with the opposition. Both sides are calling this a victory but what is very clear is that the ANC is deeply divided and that despite Chief Whip Mtembu calling for all ANC members to tow the party line 30 or more didn't. By not getting rid of Zuma the ANC are going to have a hard time at the election polls in 2019.
On Wednesday the DA called for early elections and for Parliament to be dissolved. On the legal front in September there is an Impeachment case against Zuma and in October a Criminal case.
The ANC clearly is a party divided trying everything in their power to cling onto it's legacy. They believe they can self-correct by announcing a judicial inquiry into the allegations of State Capture and with Zuma saying he will not stand again - but will he serve out his term until the 2019 elections?

Press Release:


The President, the Vote and the Battle for Power
After a record 8th no-confidence vote to remove him from office, President Jacob Zuma lives to fight another day. But with emboldened
opposition parties and internal factions dividing the party, can the ANC survive the Zuma Presidency? Carte Blanche analyses the political road
ahead.

Script:


Baleta 04 40 22 Total votes 384 the yes 177 the no 198
Upsound of cheering
Script: The whole nation was watching - President Zuma has survived his 6th parliamentary Vote of No confidence in his 8 years as president. This vote has attracted more debate and attention than any before it. A triumphant Zuma moved quickly to claim his victory
Zuma on the Parade-
Script: It was a watershed moment- the first no confidence vote held in secret - securing a far closer tally than expected. All sides emerged from Parliament feeling they had won
Holimisa” 11 19 01 00 it was a close shave and we think that the campaign by the opposition parties was well as the civil society in this country has helped
Script: It was Bantu Holimisa - Leader of the United Democratic Movement who had taken the Speaker to the constitutional court and won
John” It was noticeable during the debate that there was a lot of Defence of the ANC but not much of President Zuma
Holimisa “ no one who can publically stand up and defend Zuma . I am sure they are ashamed
Script: Julius Malema wasted no time with the press and headed straight for the waiting crowd
Malema 11 16 55 15 I am proud to be SA today because we tested our democracy and I can confirm that our democracy does work. So we are saying to Jacob Zuma passop
Script: Chief whip for the ANC Jackson Mntembu who was confident ANC MP’ would tow the party line was vindicated
11 23 23 06 Jackson ”what is important is that the motion has been defeated and of course having defeated the motion we need to deal with whatever that is a grievance sitting with the people of SA inclusive of our own members and members of parliament
MMusi 11 29 06 07 the ANC saw the removal of Zuma as the removal of the ANC as if a sec 102 motion put in the constitution is some form of coupé de ta it is not it is for the accountability of the person of the president but it is a clear indicator that the ANC now believes fundamentally that the ANC and Zuma are one
Script: Political analyst Prof Richard Calland believes in last 23 years of parliament this ranks as extremely significant momement
Richard 11 51 52 03 one shouldn’t under estimate how strong the bind in power of ANC loyalty and history is and what those ANC MPs did was break free of that and Zuma would have seen that 11 50 54 09 …he knows he is under attack from many different quarters including from within his own party and he knows his position is weakened compared with what it was he is still in office but he is not completely in power
Script: The backdrop to this momentous week was the removal from office of Finance Minister Pravin Gordhan and his deputy Mcebisi Jonas sending the rand into free fall for the second time in less than two years. Shortly afterwards South Africa’s economy was downgraded to junk status. People took to the streets in protest.
Jonas 09 25 13 24 what we need to build is a stronger civil society a movement that begins to hold Government and leaders accountable that holds political parties accountable. A weaker civil society a weaker civil movement means that Government is free to do whatever they want
Script: The Speaker of the House initially denied the call for a Secret ballot saying the Rules of Parliament did not permit it. Opposition parties challenged her in the Constitutional Court, and in June Chief Justice Mogoeng Mogoeng made a seminal ruling saying she could decide on a secret ballot if the circumstances warranted it
Link 10 24 04 07 The constitutional court ruling through detailed came down to this in a choice between the party and the constitution it’s the constitution which has to take precedence it also implored MP’s to follow their conscience
Script: In the ensuing months ANC MPs have been under enormous pressure to tow the party line and those who broke ranks and spoke out against President Zuma like Dr Makhosi Khoza have been heavily censured
makhosi 10:42 I have taken a stand- I am siding with the people and I am sorry to Mr President. I am not going to side with him.
Script: But not without great personal cost, her daughter received death threats
Khosi” Well if they had threatened me alone, maybe I would cope. Not my children.
Script: Something else that has set this vote apart is the growing civil outrage at the extent of the alleged State capture by the Gupta’s revealed through over 200 000 emails known as the Gupta’s leaks. The intricate web of deals including those between the family the president’s son Duduzane and some State owned enterprises is alleged to reveal the extent of State capture under Zuma’s presidency.
Mark 09 32 31 22 what the civil society organizations wanted to do was make su e there is an independent voice. ….there are social consequences to state capture its destroying our education system its destroying our health system
Script: Mark Heywood of Section 27 was one of 22 organizations not affiliated to any political party making their voices heard. As they set off the atmosphere was tense Baleka Mbete still had not made her decision public holding the nation in suspense right up until the 11th hour.
Baleka Mbete 00 19 26 04 Having considered all the factors and mindful of the fact that this decision is not setting a precedent I determine that voting on the motion of no confidence in the president on the 8th August 2017 cough that cough comes at a strategic …will be by Secret ballot
Script: Mbete who to date has been criticised for being partisan to the ANC caught all parties by surprise
Richard 11 43 20 13 She didn’t consult with the ANC leadership let alone the president that she made this decision and as she should do as the speaker of the house on her own and for once she … did the right thing ….the legal advice she got was absolutely unequivocal you have to grant a secret ballot in the light of the guidance of the constitutional court
Script: In a historic move Opposition parties joined forces across the country calling on the MP to do the right thing and remove Zuma. The debate in parliament was remarkably calm with ANC MP after MP defending the legacy of the ruling party. Defence Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa- Nqakula
“My conscience tells me we all need to respect the votes that brought us here. The only way the ANC can lose power is by way of a negative vote at the next general election.

Script: Malema and other Opposition parties could not persuade them otherwise

Julius 0028 34 16 “Ours today is not against the ANC but against the father of Duduzani we are here to remove Duduzani father the most corrupt individual in this country

Richard 11 39 33 the focus was supposed to be about Jacob Zuma he was hardly mentioned in the debate certainly on the ANC side this was for them about sentiment emotion and unity it was an attempt to paper over the cracks pretend that Jacob Zuma doesn’t really exist
Link 11 37 03 03 The final Tally was very close in the end and that seems to have taken many people by surprise but President Zuma remains in office so the question now becomes what lies ahead
11 29 42 40 Mmusi In September we go to court against Jacob Zuma for his charges on corruption and racketeering the 700 odd charges we will take Jacob Zuma on in Oct when the constitutional court will hear the impeachment process
Richard 11 40 24 10 over 30 ANC MPs crossed the floor defied their whip and voted with the opposition that has never happened before it was a watershed moment for me it shouldn’t be under estimated. Let’s supposed Zuma had been kicked out on Tuesday there was no consensus within the ANC about who them they would vote in to replace him as president of the country and that lack of consensus ….and the deep and bitter divisions that divide the ANC now means that it would have been hard for them to say ok we get rid of Zuma and bring in X
Script; Political scientist Professor Bheki Mngomezulu of the University of the Western Cape agrees
Bheki …..you would be in a way exposing those individuals because if you hold the position for such a short period there is very little you can do but then come Dec people will judge you on your performance within that short period so that would have been disastrous
Link 12 05 37 05 Later in the week the Democratic Alliance made it’s next move calling for the disillusion of parliament and an early election but some people have questioned the wisdom of that call
Richard 11 45 48 22 I think it is problematic because not only is it going to fail … but also it has sewed some division in the opposition ranks because the DA are going on their own on this ….thats unfortunate because the opposition have been working in quite a strategic and co-ordinated fashion in recent times
John: When the ANC says they can self- correct can we believe them
Bheki 12 29 19 02 I don’t think that handling the issue would mean recalling Zuma because in any case it’s only a few months before December so it would be unwise for the ANC leadership to recall Zuma at this point because it’s not going to benefit anyone
Richard 11 47 48 13 I think the ANC is desperate to get to December and to Midrand and to move on from the Zuma era I think there is a general recognition that so called self- correction cannot happen until he has ceased to be the President of the ANC .
Script: Jacob Zuma is not standing for re- election as ANC President in December and with as many as 8 candidates in the running it’s an indication on just how deep the divide runs within the ANC
Jonas 09 24 47 01 we should also think beyond Dec I think what we are trying to do … close the gap that was created after 1994 when Civil Society organizations were demobilised and I think the consequence of that is that political parties have actually faced a free for all
